name: Orthomolecular Medicine
description: Vitamins, minerals, and biochemical concepts central to orthomolecular and nutritional medicine.

words.hint: Linus Pauling's term meaning treating disease with the right molecule in the right amount
Administration of a nutrient at many times the standard recommended daily allowance
Chemical name for vitamin C; used in gram-level doses in orthomolecular protocols
Vitamin B3 used in high doses to lower LDL cholesterol and treat some psychiatric conditions
Essential mineral cofactor for over 300 enzymatic reactions; deficiency is very common
Trace mineral antioxidant vital for thyroid hormone metabolism and immune defense
The body's master antioxidant tripeptide that neutralizes free radicals in every cell
Biochemical process adding methyl groups; critical for mood regulation, detox, and epigenetics
Pineal hormone regulating the sleep-wake cycle; used for circadian rhythm disorders
Molecule that donates electrons to neutralize free radicals and reduce oxidative damage
Fat-soluble antioxidant essential for ATP production in mitochondria; depleted by statins
Anti-inflammatory polyunsaturated fatty acids found in fish oil; EPA and DHA
Trace mineral essential for immune function, wound healing, and over 200 enzymes
Vitamin B9 critical for DNA synthesis and prevention of neural tube defects in pregnancy
Vitamin B6 involved in amino acid metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis
Vitamin B2 essential for energy metabolism and recycling of the antioxidant glutathione
Vitamin B1 essential for carbohydrate metabolism and nerve function; deficient in alcoholism
Synthetic form of vitamin B12 used to correct deficiency and prevent neurological damage
Chemical name for vitamin E; fat-soluble antioxidant that protects cell membranes from oxidation
Plant pigment that converts to vitamin A and acts as a lipid-phase antioxidant
Plant-derived polyphenol that works synergistically with vitamin C to strengthen capillaries
B vitamin-like nutrient involved in cell signaling; used at high doses for mood disorders
Essential amino acid that is the precursor to serotonin and melatonin in the brain
Low-dose mineral salt used in orthomolecular psychiatry for mood stabilization
Imbalance between free radical production and antioxidant defenses leading to cellular damage
Essential vitamin or mineral required in small amounts for normal physiological function
Fraction of an ingested nutrient that is actually absorbed and utilized by the body
Cellular organelles producing ATP energy; a key therapeutic target in orthomolecular medicine
Two-time Nobel laureate who founded orthomolecular medicine and championed vitamin C therapy
Overworked adrenal glands from chronic stress; treated with vitamin C and B5 repletion
